plan.topic: Tirzepatide and semaglutide: 5 common myths, each corrected with trial evidence
plan.angle:
Preferably make this a Short: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) & semaglutide: 3 myths the trials corrected', with each fact tagged to its drug, trial and population.

If it stays a carousel:
- Slide 1: SELECT (semaglutide), with absolute and relative rates.
- Slide 2: SURMOUNT-1 body scan (tirzepatide, 124 vs 36), with the kidney and 'start gently' caveats.
- Slide 3: per-drug trial averages with their populations.
- Slide 4: dated FDA warning on unapproved products, with retatrutide investigational as of Oct 2026.
- Slide 5: per-drug label wording on GI effects.
- Last slide: disclaimer, 'Don't stop or change your medicines on your own', and the full prescriber line.

plan.why:
Covers the myth-busting share of the mix with a list people save. Carousels reach only 0–3 accounts, so this is a low-cost format that reuses already-verified facts. | fact-check: The myths are accurate and safe, but it's a carousel, and all 19 carousels have reached 0–3 accounts. The playbook says to rebuild good carousel topics as Shorts or Reels, so consider moving this to a Short.

Scope fixes if it goes ahead:
- Myth 1: SELECT studied semaglutide only, in adults with heart disease and overweight or obesity without diabetes. Don't let the fact imply tirzepatide. Give the absolute rates (about 6.5% vs 8.0%) next to the roughly 20% relative reduction, copied from NEJM 2023.
- Myth 2: the SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy is tirzepatide only. Keep 124 vs 36 and 'about three-quarters fat', plus the kidney caveat and 'start gently'.
- Myth 3: give each trial average with its own drug and population, and don't merge STEP and SURMOUNT numbers.
- Myth 4: retatrutide is investigational as of Oct 2026. Credit the FDA warning about unapproved products, date it, and name no sellers.
- Myth 5: quote each drug's own label on GI effects during dose escalation, with no dosing.

package.title: Tirzepatide & Semaglutide: 5 Myths vs What the Trials Show

social.instagram_caption:
Myth vs. the actual trials: tirzepatide and semaglutide in adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition (SELECT: heart disease plus overweight/obesity, no diabetes), checked against the published numbers.

Swipe through 5 common myths:
• "Semaglutide only moves the scale" — SELECT: adults with heart disease + overweight/obesity, no diabetes, ~40 months' average follow-up. Heart attack, stroke or cardiovascular death: 6.5% on semaglutide 2.4 mg vs 8.0% on placebo (~20% lower relative risk).
• "Tirzepatide weight loss is mostly muscle" — SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy (124 on tirzepatide, all doses pooled, vs 36 on placebo, 72 weeks): about three-quarters of the weight lost on tirzepatide was fat; some lean mass was also lost.
• "Both drugs give identical results" — STEP 1 and SURMOUNT-1 are separate trials, not head-to-head. Averages, not promises.
• "Stomach side effects never ease up" — mostly mild to moderate in both trials. On semaglutide (STEP 1) they were typically transient and subsided with time; on tirzepatide (SURMOUNT-1) they occurred mainly during dose escalation. Severe or not easing? Tell your prescriber.
• "Research" retatrutide isn't the trial drug — it's investigational and not FDA-approved (as of Oct 2026). FDA says it has warned companies that illegally sold unapproved retatrutide products falsely labeled "for research purposes" (FDA, current as of Oct 1, 2026).

We checked 5 common tirzepatide and semaglutide myths against the actual published trials — SELECT, STEP 1 and SURMOUNT-1 — in adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition (SELECT: heart disease plus overweight/obesity, without diabetes).

A few highlights: in SELECT (adults with heart disease and overweight/obesity, without diabetes, about 40 months' average follow-up), 6.5% on semaglutide 2.4 mg vs 8.0% on placebo had a heart attack, stroke or cardiovascular death, about a 20% lower relative risk. In the SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy (124 on tirzepatide, all doses pooled, vs 36 on placebo, 72 weeks), about three-quarters of the weight lost on tirzepatide was fat; some lean mass was also lost. Stomach side effects such as nausea and diarrhea were the most common, mostly mild to moderate. We also cover why "research" retatrutide isn't the trial drug: retatrutide is investigational and not FDA-approved (as of Oct 2026), and FDA says it has warned companies that illegally sold unapproved retatrutide products falsely labeled "for research purposes" (FDA, current as of Oct 1, 2026). Use only medicines your prescriber prescribes.

factcheck.summary: I checked every number and description against the sources, and they hold up. SELECT: 6.5% vs 8.0%, 8,803 vs 8,801 people, about 20% lower relative risk, about 40 months' average follow-up, correct population. SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy (DOM 2025, confirmed on PMC): 124 people on tirzepatide vs 36 on placebo, fat −33.9% vs −8.2%, lean −10.9% vs −2.6%, about 75% of the weight lost was fat. STEP 1: 14.9% vs 2.4% at 68 weeks, 1,306 vs 655 people. SURMOUNT-1: 20.9% vs 3.1% at 72 weeks, 630 vs 643 people. The stomach side-effect wording matches each trial's published abstract. The FDA page (current as of Oct 1, 2026) does name retatrutide among products falsely labeled 'for research purposes' or 'not for human consumption'. The safety caveats are all there: kidney disease for protein, start gently for exercise, fluid limits, the prescriber line and the disclaimer. The cross-trial comparison is clearly marked as separate trials, not head-to-head. Three wording fixes are optional: match the FDA's own wording on slide 7, give the full population on slide 5, and change 'trial-checked' on the hook slide because the retatrutide slide is checked against the FDA, not a trial.

issues.claim: FDA warns that some companies illegally sell unapproved drugs containing retatrutide that are falsely labeled 'for research purposes' or 'not for human consumption'
issues.problem: The FDA page says the agency 'has warned companies that have illegally sold' these products, which means it sent warning letters. The slide's wording makes it sound like a present-tense warning to the public, so the FDA is credited with something slightly different from what it wrote.
issues.fix: Retatrutide is investigational and not FDA-approved (as of Oct 2026). FDA says it has warned companies that illegally sold unapproved drugs containing retatrutide that were falsely labeled 'for research purposes' or 'not for human consumption' (FDA, current as of Oct 1, 2026). These aren't the trial drug. Use only medicines your prescriber prescribes.

issues.claim: adults with obesity or overweight without diabetes
issues.problem: In both STEP 1 and SURMOUNT-1, overweight adults had to have at least one weight-related condition to take part. Slide 3 already says this correctly, so slide 5 should match.
issues.fix: Average % of body weight lost, adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes. STEP 1 (68 weeks): semaglutide 2.4 mg, 1,306 people vs placebo, 655. SURMOUNT-1 (72 weeks): tirzepatide 15 mg, 630 people vs placebo, 643. Separate trials, not head-to-head.

issues.problem: The fifth myth (retatrutide) is checked against an FDA statement, not trial data. It's also about retatrutide, not tirzepatide or semaglutide, so the hook slightly over-promises.
